discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: LIGO opened the audio band of the gravitational-wave spectrum. Pulsar timing arrays have now opened the nanohertz band, turning the Galaxy's millisecond pulsars into a detector the size of a galaxy. In 2023 NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA each reported evidence for a stochastic gravitational-wave background showing the Hellings-Downs angular correlation, which is the signature of spacetime itself being disturbed. The signal most likely comes from the cosmic population of supermassive black-hole binaries, and it constrains new physics in the early universe. McLaughlin and Siemens built NANOGrav into a Physics Frontiers Center and led its instrumentation, timing and data-analysis program. Siemens brought LIGO-style detection statistics to the work, including careful significance estimates. Kramer's precision pulsar timing and leadership of the European effort were essential. Together they have made pulsar timing a gravitational-wave observatory, and a new window on black-hole growth across cosmic time.
